title: From the stairs to the stars
caption: The Milky Way and laser guide stars over the Auxiliary Telescope stairs, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A staircase at ESO's Paranal Observatory leads up toward a sky thick with stars. The galactic center can, at first glance, pass for a dragon with a strange orange tongue. Bright yellow beams cross the scene. They are laser guide stars fired from the Very Large Telescope (VLT), which stands to the right, just outside the frame.

The lasers create artificial stars high in the atmosphere. The telescope's adaptive optics system uses them to correct for atmospheric blurring and make the sharpest possible observations from the ground. For the VLT, this is simply an ordinary night's work.

The stairs give outside access to the VLT's smaller Auxiliary Telescopes, and they make a fine spot for photography. Standing at the top, at 2635 meters above sea level plus some twenty steps, you can see a wealth of stars that stay hidden elsewhere, because Paranal has the darkest skies of any major observatory on Earth.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph credited to F. Millour/ESO. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the Milky Way's colors and dust may look more vivid here than to someone on the stairs.

explore: Short of traveling to space, ESO suggests, few places make you feel closer to the stars than the top of this staircase in Chile's Atacama Desert, where the sky feels just one small step beyond the last stair.
alt: A staircase leading up toward a star-filled sky, with the center of the Milky Way above and bright yellow laser beams crossing it.
